title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
prompt:
Given a string `s` (uppercase letters) and an integer `k`, you may change at most `k` characters. Return the length of the longest substring you can make consist of a single repeated letter.

**Example**: `s = "AABABBA"`, `k = 1` → `4` (change one B in `"AABA"` → `"AAAA"`, or one A in `"ABBA"`).

Window validity: `windowLength - countOfMostFrequentChar <= k` (the others get replaced).
hints: Keep an `int[26]` of counts inside the window; track `maxCount` = highest single-letter count seen in the window.
Window invalid when `(r - l + 1) - maxCount > k` → remove s.charAt(l), l++.
maxCount can be left stale after shrinking — the answer only grows when a genuinely better window appears, so it still works (a subtle, famous detail).

solution.explanation: O(n). A window is fixable when its minority characters number ≤ k. `maxCount` is allowed to go stale on shrink: a stale (too-high) maxCount only makes the window look better than it is, and the recorded best from when it was genuinely valid still stands — the answer is never overstated beyond a previously achieved size.
